blindSummary:
This state/province led the national statistics for 2025 with 7 recorded killings of LGBT+ people; trans women constituted 58.3% of all such killings nationwide that year, across at least 17 states reporting victims. Its legal-gender-recognition law (2021) keeps an 18-year minimum-age requirement that the country's supreme court voided in March 2022, yet the state congress has still not corrected the text - legislative non-compliance with a final court ruling is itself a hostility signal directly relevant to a visitor whose documents must match presentation. There is no dedicated investigative machinery, no transfeminicide offence, and no state-level enforcement data.

The combination of top-of-table lethality and open defiance of the judiciary distinguishes this state/province from states that simply lack statutes: here a statute exists but the legislature actively refuses to conform it to a binding ruling. For context elsewhere: the country's capital, which also had high counts in 2024-25, created a transfeminicide investigation unit and mandatory-response protocol within months; the country's most populous state, which likewise defies a supreme-court ruling on recognition, has at least had a penal-code hate-crime provision covering bias motives since 2021. This state/province has neither the court-compliant text nor any criminal-law protection or enforcement innovation.

An international human-rights organisation's feature on state gender-recognition laws in the country (March 2025): this state/province enacted its legal gender recognition law in 2021 but with an 18-year age requirement the country's supreme court declared unconstitutional in March 2022; the state congress has not amended the text since; the feature maps which of the 32 states had (and had not) legislated a recognition procedure by March 2025, and links document mismatch to police questioning risk for trans people.
